chapter: Joe Lyde stories and bandstand tales
title: Joe Lyde: Negro funerals, showmanship and the beer-glass mute
summary: Zanco hasn't been to a Black funeral, but Joe Lyde marched in them and Zulu. Zanco recalls Lyde's showmanship, beer-glass mute and odd dress.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: Have you been to many, uh, parades that the Negro bands were playing? Uh, uh, on socials?

No, I can't say that I have. I think I maybe one of the few that live in New Orleans that hadn't been to a Negro funeral. You've never been there any. Uh, from what I can understand, uh, this boy, Joe Lyde, that used to play con-ed with the, uh, Last Straws, he'd march with the Negro, uh, parades already at funerals. He'd, uh, he'd march with them.
Mardi Gras, he was, uh. He played the Zulu. He played the Zulu parade almost all the way through then.
Yeah. She could get Miss Hon, Kid She could talk about that. And then he played Arthur Ogles funeral, too, you know.

Well, you know, all in all, uh, Joe Lyde, Joe Lyde was, wasn't only a musician. He was a pretty good entertainer while he was sitting on a bandstand. Uh, you know, and that's, that's why I always felt I had a big pair of shoes to fill when I went in this group. Cause, uh, as far as a showman, I mean, I'm nothing to look at, you know. But Joe, Joe would put on a flow show and play. Well, Joe went beyond and I paid him on something.
You know, he got too wild.

Well, you know, um, I, I, that's the first time I've seen that. Uh, one night, uh, they were playing a job someplace. Joe was, uh, playing connet and I just happened to be at this particular place. And Joe needed a mute for one of the tunes he was playing. So he had a half glass of beer sitting on a table. So he picks a glass up, throws the bell on the floor and uses the glass for a mute. And I mean, you know, you just don't see things like that every place, you know. But, uh, it was, it was real effective and I, I've used it several times myself. I used a plain drinking glass for a mute.
That just shows, uh, how Joe had, at one time, a one track mind. See, any other trumpet playing a little drop of beer.
That's right. I seen Joe show up for a job with a blue sock on an orange sock one time. No shoes. With the sandals.
Dressed to kill, but he had a pair of sandals on. Yeah. Joe just didn't care. All he cared for was to play his music, see.
